clue.text: Savoury snacks child tucks into, not the genuine article

indicators.note: the child is pictured eating, but tucking into something here means going inside it

parts.note: pasties are pastry turnovers with a savoury filling, a British bakery staple

explanation.surface: A child eats meat pies, which turn out to be fakes rather than the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating, but it signals going inside. A pasty is a folded pastry case with a savoury filling, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastiches are imitations of another work or style, so they are not originals.

clue.text: For instance, clutch ring inlaid with diamonds

indicators.note: something inlaid has another piece set into it, so one letter goes inside the ring word

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A clutch bag or a ring set with diamonds suggests jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clutch' and 'ring' suggest a handbag and jewellery; here clutch is a car's foot control and ring a bell sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's clutch is operated by the foot, so it is one example of a pedal.

clue.text: Contrary chap, say, probing food item on a bill?

indicators.note: contrary means the whole build is read the opposite way, backwards
the chap and say letters are pushed into the food word

parts.note: eats is a casual word for food
a man is a chap
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: An awkward man pokes at a dish listed on a restaurant bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' reverses the whole build (EMANEGATS). The bill is a theatre playbill, not a restaurant one.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's professional name is printed on a playbill, so it is an item on a bill.

clue.text: Joins players from Milan on golf course

parts.note: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club
links is a golf course, especially one by the sea

explanation.surface: An Italian footballer signs up at a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlink things is to connect them, so interlinks means joins.

clue.text: But we must supplant president's last love

indicators.note: to supplant is to replace, so the two letters take the place of one letter in the name

parts.note: Herbert Hoover was a president of the United States
love is zero in tennis, so O; last picks the second O of the president's name

explanation.surface: We must replace a president's final sweetheart, but on what terms?
explanation.walkthrough: In HOOVER the second O is replaced by WE.
explanation.definitionFit: However and but are both conjunctions introducing a contrast, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Bowler, wayward type harnessing a touch of pace

indicators.note: harnessing means holding in, so the first letter goes inside the wayward word

parts.note: a sinner is someone who strays from right conduct

indicators.note: a touch is only a little, so just the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler, a bit of a rogue, adds some pace to his deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a spinner is a bowler who makes the ball turn rather than relying on speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner is a type of cricket bowler who imparts spin to the ball.

clue.text: Abandon attempt to get to game

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away or abandon it
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: Someone gives up trying to reach a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game played with cards, so it is one example of a game.

clue.text: Complain as book price rises

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word is read from the bottom up, backwards

parts.note: a fee is a price charged

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles as the cost of a book goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is informal slang for to grumble or complain.

clue.text: Green water often bottled up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Evian is a French mineral water usually sold in bottles

explanation.surface: Environmentally minded water is frequently sealed into bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like environmental; it means inexperienced. 'up' reverses EVIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or unsophisticated, which is what naive means.

clue.text: Successive balls received and struck (with attack)

parts.note: in cricket, an over is a run of six successive balls from one bowler
taken means received

explanation.surface: A batter faces a series of deliveries and is hit by an aggressive one.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled in a row by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overtaken by an illness or fit is to be suddenly struck by an attack of it.

clue.text: Cask beer picked up for military detachment

indicators.note: what is picked up is heard, so the beer word is taken as it sounds when said

parts.note: draught beer is drawn from a cask or keg rather than bottled

explanation.surface: Some barrels of ale are collected for the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' is a hearing signal: DRAUGHT and DRAFT are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a group of soldiers detached from a larger body for a special duty.

clue.text: Spooner's low-alcohol drink a boon to errant drivers

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening sounds of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: light drinks are those with less alcohol
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A weak wine might help drivers who wander, since they stay soberer.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of LIGHT WINE gives the sound of WHITE LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted road marking keeps straying motorists in their lane, so it helps drivers who wander.

clue.text: Never lie to angry clubman

indicators.note: angry suggests agitation, so the letters of the three words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction never to deceive someone who is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angry' signals the anagram of NEVER LIE TO. Lee Trevino is a Mexican-American golfer, a six-time major winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer carries golf clubs, so a famous golf professional is cryptically a clubman.

clue.text: Standard breached by Catholic faction

indicators.note: a wall breached by something has that thing forced into it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a set pattern is a standard or fixed one

explanation.surface: A principle is undermined by a Catholic splinter group.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a breakaway religious or political group, which is a kind of faction.

clue.text: Extraordinary rendition transporting a suspect

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or unsound, so the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Rendition flights carry a terror suspect in an unusual operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary rendition' reads as one phrase but splits: the definition, then RENDITION plus A, made into an anagram by 'suspect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means excessive or beyond normal limits, so it means extraordinary.

clue.text: Adult in his own field carrying more weight

indicators.note: the adult letter is placed in the field word

parts.note: a métier is one's own trade or area of expertise
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up working in his own speciality gains weight or influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meatier is more substantial, with more weight or substance to it.

clue.text: Modern Miss guarding flower in Wales grew fragrant blooms

indicators.note: the title's two letters stand around the river and grew words

parts.note: Ms is the modern title used instead of Miss
a flower is a river, something that flows; the Usk is a river in Wales
rose means grew or increased

explanation.surface: A young woman protects a Welsh plant that gave off scented flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, so a river: the Usk in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Musk roses are a climbing rose species with strongly scented flowers.

clue.text: Managed to fire rifle

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed
to sack someone is to fire them

explanation.surface: Someone managed to shoot a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' and 'fire' suggest guns, but rifle is the verb, meaning to search through and rob.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search it hastily and plunder it, just as to ransack it.

clue.text: A criminal securing crooked mate's remission

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the criminal word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: bent is slang for corrupt or criminal

indicators.note: crooked means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a mate is a friend; the possessive leaves the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A villain holds onto a dishonest friend's pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' makes ATEM, which 'securing' places within the criminal word; 'crooked' and 'criminal' both look like descriptions of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Abatement and remission both mean a reduction, as of a tax or penalty.

clue.text: Summit goes into matter, turning sound off

indicators.note: the summit word is placed inside the other
turning means the word for matter is read backwards

parts.note: pus is matter from an infected wound
a peak is a summit

explanation.surface: A mountaintop enters into a subject, which then switches off its noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' gives SUP, which 'goes into' then opens to take the summit. 'matter' means pus, not a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound off is to voice one's opinion loudly, as one does when talking without holding back.

clue.text: Mundane master, so it appears, inspiring article

parts.note: a pro is an expert, a master of a skill

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the article is taken inside

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to show a quotation is printed as it appears
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dull expert apparently gives an essay life.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC, Latin for 'thus', marks a quoted error as being in the original.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull and ordinary, lacking poetry, so it means mundane.

clue.text: Understanding landlord's profit?

parts.note: a pub landlord's place of work is the bar
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A wry question about the profit a pub landlord makes.
explanation.walkthrough: A British pub landlord runs the bar, so his profit is a bar gain.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is an agreement or deal, the understanding struck between two parties.

clue.text: Sharp tail of garden bird

parts.note: bitter means sharp in taste

indicators.note: the tail is the end, so the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A pointed tail of a garden bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like wading bird of reedbeds.

clue.text: Clarets, perhaps, or their Premiership rivals?

definitions.meaning: claret is a red wine from Bordeaux, so clarets are examples of red wines
Burnley FC are nicknamed the Clarets, and Liverpool and Manchester United, rival Premier League clubs

explanation.surface: A football fan's question about which team is the Clarets' rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clarets is Burnley's nickname in English football; Liverpool and Manchester United, both called the Reds, play them in the Premier League.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarets are red wines, and the Reds is the nickname of rival football clubs.

clue.text: Third of Tories wearing blue go under

indicators.note: the letter is wearing the other word as clothing, so it is wrapped inside it

parts.note: blue means sad or down

indicators.note: picks the third letter of the word

explanation.surface: A third of Conservatives in their party's blue colours lose an election.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so the surface links Tories to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown is to sink beneath water and die, to go under.

clue.text: Bulk transport lines supplying crates

indicators.note: to crate something is to enclose it, so these words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Large shipments travel along transport routes that provide packing cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crates' looks like a noun for packing cases but is a verb: the words enclose the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Portliness is stoutness of body, so it means bulk in the sense of a large build.

clue.text: What archaeologists may find strenuous, spades to the fore

indicators.note: to the fore means at the front, so the spades letter goes first

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
hard work is strenuous

explanation.surface: Archaeologists' digging is hard work, with spades leading the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a broken piece of pottery, a typical find at a dig.

clue.text: Fine wine unopened

indicators.note: a thing unopened has not had its start, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: A good wine is left sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' drops the first letter of TOKAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means acceptable or all right, which fine also means.

clue.text: Effect from explosion of wine and whiskey kept in store

indicators.note: the wine and whiskey letters are kept inside the store word

parts.note: to save something is to store it
hock is a white wine from Germany
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet code word for the letter W

explanation.surface: Bottles of wine and whiskey stored away might cause a blast.
explanation.walkthrough: Hock is a white German wine, formerly popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A blast sends out a high-pressure front of air through its surroundings, which is one effect of an explosion.

clue.text: Youth leader makes plan, not taking sides

indicators.note: sides are outer letters, so dropping them from each word leaves only the inside letters

explanation.surface: A head of a youth group draws up a plan while staying neutral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not taking sides' looks like neutrality but strips the end letters from MAKES and PLAN, leaving AKE and LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Akela is the title given to the adult leader of a Cub Scout pack.

clue.text: Cheerful star, nominally on vacation

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: something vacated is emptied, so the word loses its contents and only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A cheerful celebrity, in name only, goes on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny disposition is cheerful and bright.

clue.text: Cheerful jailbird temporarily housed?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a jailbird
people living in tents are temporarily housed, so they are tented

explanation.surface: A happy prisoner is only staying briefly in lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being contented is being happy and satisfied, a close synonym of cheerful.
